name: Pokhara & the Middle Hills
tagline: Lakes, ridges and hill bazaars below Annapurna
meta_description: Pokhara tours and the Middle Hills: Phewa Lake, Sarangkot sunrise, paragliding, Bandipur, Manakamana, Gorkha and short hikes, with prices in INR and USD.
summary: Pokhara and the Middle Hills cover the lake city at 822 m and the ridges around it: Sarangkot sunrise, paragliding over Phewa Lake, the Newar bazaar of Bandipur, Manakamana's cable car temple and Gorkha's hilltop palace. Plan three to six nights, best from October to March, with no trekking permit needed for most sights.
intro: Pokhara sits in a broad valley about 200 km west of Kathmandu, 25 minutes by air or 6–8 hours by road. What sets it apart is how close the snow comes: Machhapuchhre, 6,993 m, rises about 30 km north of Phewa Lake, with Annapurna South, Annapurna II and Lamjung Himal beside it and Dhaulagiri further west. Lakeside, the 3 km strip of hotels and cafes on Phewa's eastern shore, is where almost every visitor stays, and it is within 45 minutes of every sight in the valley.

Around the city the land climbs in green steps. Sarangkot, at about 1,600 m, is the dawn viewpoint and the launch field for tandem paragliders. The World Peace Pagoda looks back over the lake from the south shore at about 1,100 m. North-west of town, a 45-minute drive and a short climb lead to Australian Camp at about 2,060 m and the Gurung village of Dhampus, while Panchase, at 2,517 m the highest point we cover in this region, offers a quieter overnight walk through orchid forest.

East along the Prithvi Highway lie the Middle Hills that many Kathmandu–Pokhara itineraries pass straight through. Bandipur, 8 km up a side road from Dumre, is a car-free Newar trading town of brick houses at about 1,030 m. Manakamana's Bhagwati temple sits on a ridge at 1,302 m, reached in about 10 minutes by Nepal's first passenger cable car from Kurintar. Gorkha, a 24 km detour north from Abu Khaireni, is where Prithvi Narayan Shah began the unification of Nepal from a hilltop palace.

For Indian families and couples the region is the heart of most Nepal tours: three nights in Pokhara, often joined to Kathmandu, Chitwan or a night in Bandipur. For adventure seekers it holds paragliding, the ZipFlyer zipline, ultralight flights and bungee at Hemja. For trekkers it is the start of the Annapurna trails. Our packages here run from 3 to 6 nights, with 3-star Lakeside hotels up to Fish Tail Lodge and Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge.

highlights.title: Phewa Lake at first light
highlights.text: Hire a painted wooden doonga at the Barahi ghat before 8 am, when the water is still enough to mirror Machhapuchhre. Five minutes out lies the island temple of Tal Barahi; a longer 20–30 minute row reaches the south shore trail up to the World Peace Pagoda at about 1,100 m.

highlights.title: Sarangkot sunrise and paragliding
highlights.text: A 30–45 minute pre-dawn drive puts you on the Sarangkot ridge at about 1,600 m as Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre catch the sun. Later the same morning the slope below becomes a launch field, and tandem flights of 20–30 minutes glide down to land beside Phewa Lake.

highlights.title: Bandipur's car-free Newar bazaar
highlights.text: Bandipur grew rich in the 19th century on the trade route between India and Tibet, and its main street of three-storey brick houses, carved windows and stone paving is closed to cars. Stay a night to walk up to Thani Mai at dawn and see the Annapurna and Manaslu ranges from the ridge.

highlights.title: Manakamana cable car and temple
highlights.text: The 2.8 km cable car from Kurintar on the Trishuli river climbs about 1,000 m to Manakamana in roughly 10 minutes. At the top, the two-roofed Bhagwati temple draws Hindu pilgrims who believe the goddess grants wishes; Saturdays and Dashain bring queues of an hour or more for darshan.

highlights.title: Gorkha Durbar and the birth of Nepal
highlights.text: On a ridge about 300 m above Gorkha bazaar, the fortified palace and Kalika temple mark the seat from which Prithvi Narayan Shah set out in the 18th century to unify Nepal. The climb of roughly 1,500 stone steps takes about an hour, rewarded with views of Manaslu and Himalchuli on clear days.

highlights.title: Short hikes and village stays
highlights.text: Australian Camp, about 2,060 m, is a 1–1.5 hour climb from Kande, with Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre straight ahead at dawn. Dhampus and Sirubari offer Gurung homestays with home-cooked dal bhat and cultural evenings, and the ridge walk between Begnas and Rupa lakes fills a quiet half day.

getting_there: Most visitors reach Pokhara from Kathmandu. Buddha Air, Yeti Airlines and Shree Airlines fly the route many times a day in about 25 minutes to Pokhara International Airport, which opened in January 2023 east of the old airfield; morning departures are the most reliable. By road the Prithvi Highway runs about 200 km via Mugling and Damauli, 6–8 hours by private car and 7–9 hours by tourist bus, with Manakamana and Bandipur close to the route. From India, the Sonauli–Bhairahawa border is about 190 km and 7–8 hours away on the Siddhartha Highway through Butwal and Syangja. Chitwan's Sauraha is about 155 km and 4.5–5.5 hours by road. Pokhara's airport has had only a handful of scheduled international services, so check current status before you travel.
permits: Pokhara city, Sarangkot, the World Peace Pagoda, Begnas Lake, Bandipur, Manakamana and Gorkha need no trekking permit, only small site tickets. Australian Camp and Dhampus lie inside the Annapurna Conservation Area, so walkers need an ACAP entry permit: NPR 3,000 for foreign nationals and NPR 1,000 for SAARC nationals, including Indians. Since 2023 Nepal's rules have required foreign trekkers in conservation areas to walk with a licensed guide, though enforcement on these short trails has varied. Panchase lies outside ACAP; local forest fees may apply. Check current status before you travel.

months.weather: Pokhara 7 to 20 °C, dry, morning mist on the lake
months.summary: January is cold at dawn and bright by day, with some of the clearest mountain views of the year once the morning mist over Phewa burns off around 9 am. The Pokhara Street Festival ends on 1 January, so the first day of the month is lively at Lakeside before the town settles into a quiet, good-value fortnight. Sarangkot sunrises are sharp but close to freezing, and Bandipur's ridge is crisp and clear.
months.tip: Bring a down jacket for the Sarangkot sunrise, where it can be near 0 °C before the sun appears.

months.weather: Pokhara 9 to 23 °C, mostly dry, warming afternoons
months.summary: February is one of the best value months in the region. Days warm to the low 20s, skies are usually clear and hotel rates sit below the October peak. It is good for the Australian Camp and Dhampus overnight walk, with the first rhododendrons opening on the ridges late in the month. Paragliding runs on most days, and Manakamana and Gorkha are pleasant for pilgrims and history-minded travellers before the spring heat.
months.tip: Book February dates for Pokhara if you want clear peaks without October's prices and crowds.

months.weather: Pokhara 12 to 27 °C, warm, haze building late in the month
months.summary: March brings warm days and red rhododendrons on the hills around Panchase and Australian Camp. Mornings are usually clear, though haze from dust and crop burning softens the views by mid-afternoon and becomes heavier towards April. Thermals are strong, so paragliders often fly longer cross-country routes. It is a good month for the Panchase overnight hike, for Begnas Lake and for a combined Bandipur and Pokhara road trip.
months.tip: Plan mountain photography for the first two hours after sunrise in March, before the haze rises.

months.summary: April is warm and often hazy, with mountain views reliable only in the early morning and short thunderstorms building some afternoons. Nepali New Year falls in mid-April and fills Pokhara with domestic visitors. The lakes are the best part of the month: early rows on Phewa and Begnas, and swims in hotel pools. Indian school holidays begin late in the month, so book family rooms ahead.
months.tip: Choose a hotel with a pool for April and May, when Lakeside afternoons reach 30 °C.

months.summary: May is hot and humid in the valley, with pre-monsoon cloud hiding the peaks on many days and evening storms becoming common. It remains busy with Indian families on summer holidays, who use the cooler hill stays as a break from the plains. Bandipur, Sirubari and Dhampus are a few degrees cooler than Lakeside. Paragliding continues, though cloud cancels more slots than in spring.
months.tip: Book paragliding for the first morning slot in May, before cloud builds over Sarangkot.

months.weather: Pokhara 21 to 30 °C, monsoon arrives mid-June, heavy rain
months.summary: The monsoon usually reaches Pokhara in mid-June, and the valley is one of the wettest places in Nepal. Rain falls mostly in long evening and night downpours, leaving green, hazy days with the mountains hidden. Landslides begin to affect the Prithvi Highway and hill roads. Indoor sights still work: the International Mountain Museum, Gupteshwor Cave and Gorkha's museum. Hotel rates drop sharply.
months.tip: Fly rather than drive between Kathmandu and Pokhara in the monsoon to avoid landslide delays on the highway.

months.weather: Pokhara 22 to 29 °C, wettest month, frequent cloud
months.summary: July is the wettest month, when Pokhara can receive close to 900 mm of rain. The mountains rarely show, paragliding and ultralight flights are mostly paused, and the Australian Camp trail brings leeches. Davis Falls and the Seti gorge are at their most powerful, and the rice terraces are bright green. We suggest a short stay focused on the lake, caves and temples, with flexible plans for road travel.
months.tip: Travel insurance with trip interruption cover is worth having for monsoon travel in Nepal.

months.weather: Pokhara 22 to 30 °C, heavy rain, clearer spells late
months.summary: August stays wet, with some clear mornings late in the month. Teej, the women's festival, usually falls between mid-August and mid-September, and on the main day Pokhara's women in red saris queue at Tal Barahi and Bindhyabasini. Pilgrims still travel to Manakamana by cable car, which runs in most weather. Road delays remain common, so allow a spare day either side of long drives.
months.tip: Ask us for the Teej date in your year, as it follows the lunar calendar and moves each August or September.

months.weather: Pokhara 21 to 29 °C, rain easing, clearer late
months.summary: September is the shoulder month. Rain eases through the month, mornings clear more often and the hills are at their greenest, with rice ripening on the terraces around Begnas and Sirubari. Paragliding operators restart regular flights as the monsoon fades. Teej sometimes falls in early September, and Dashain often begins at the end of the month or in October. Late September gives good value before peak rates.
months.tip: Late September departures often get green terraces, clearing skies and lower hotel rates.

months.weather: Pokhara 17 to 27 °C, dry, clear and settled
months.summary: October is the peak month. Skies are clear, the air is washed by the monsoon and almost every morning shows the full Annapurna range from Sarangkot and the lake. Dashain, and often Tihar, fall in this period, so Nepali families travel home and fill buses, flights and hotels. Paragliding slots sell out, and Bandipur's few hotels book early. Gorkha and Manakamana are crowded on festival days.
months.tip: Reserve flights, paragliding and Bandipur rooms early for October, when Dashain travel fills seats.

months.weather: Pokhara 12 to 24 °C, very clear, cool mornings
months.summary: November is often the clearest month, with crisp air, cool mornings and warm afternoons around 24 °C. It suits every outing in the region: Sarangkot dawn, the Panchase hike, Phewa rowing and the World Peace Pagoda at sunset. Tihar, the festival of lights, often falls in early November, when houses in the Old Bazaar and Bandipur glow with oil lamps. Crowds ease after mid-month.
months.tip: Carry a warm layer for November dawns, which drop to about 10 °C in Pokhara and lower on the ridges.

months.weather: Pokhara 8 to 21 °C, dry, clear days, cold nights
months.summary: December is dry and clear, with the sharpest mountain views of the year and cold nights. Christmas and New Year bring Indian families back to Lakeside, and the Pokhara Street Festival closes the main road from 28 December for five days of food stalls and music. Australian Camp and Dhampus are excellent but cold after dark, and Bandipur's sunrise from Thani Mai is at its clearest.
months.tip: Book Lakeside hotels for the last week of December two months ahead, as the street festival fills the town.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Pokhara and the Middle Hills?
faqs.a: Three nights in Pokhara covers Phewa Lake, Sarangkot sunrise, the caves, the World Peace Pagoda and a paragliding flight. Add a night in Bandipur on the drive from Kathmandu, and a half-day stop at Manakamana, for a 5–6 night trip. Hikers can add one or two nights at Australian Camp, Dhampus or Panchase. Gorkha fits as a detour of half a day.

faqs.q: What is the best way to go from Kathmandu to Pokhara?
faqs.a: Fly if time matters or you travel with elderly parents: the flight takes about 25 minutes and costs roughly US$ 100–130 for foreigners, less for Indian nationals. Drive if you want Manakamana or Bandipur on the way: the 200 km road takes 6–8 hours by car. Tourist buses take 7–9 hours and are the cheapest option.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Pokhara?
faqs.a: October to December gives the clearest mountain views, dry weather and days of 20–27 °C. February and March are also very good, with spring flowers but more haze by April. June to August is the monsoon, when Pokhara gets some of Nepal's heaviest rain, the peaks hide and paragliding is mostly paused. September is a good-value shoulder month.

faqs.q: How much does a Pokhara tour package cost from India?
faqs.a: Our 3-night Pokhara package starts at about ₹16,000 per person on twin sharing with a 3-star Lakeside hotel, breakfast and a private car. A 4-night family holiday starts near ₹21,000, a 4-night honeymoon at Temple Tree and Fish Tail Lodge near ₹34,000, and the 6-night Kathmandu, Bandipur and Pokhara tour near ₹36,000. Flights from India are extra.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to visit Pokhara?
faqs.a: No permit is needed for Pokhara, Sarangkot, Begnas Lake, Bandipur, Manakamana or Gorkha; you pay only small site tickets. Short hikes to Australian Camp and Dhampus enter the Annapurna Conservation Area and need an ACAP permit, NPR 1,000 for Indians and NPR 3,000 for other foreigners. Guide rules have changed since 2023, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Bandipur worth a stop between Kathmandu and Pokhara?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have one extra night. Bandipur is 8 km off the highway at Dumre, about 5–6 hours from Kathmandu and 2.5–3 hours from Pokhara, so it splits the drive neatly. The car-free bazaar, Thani Mai sunrise and Siddha Gufa cave fill an afternoon and a morning. A quick lunch stop also works, but the town is best in the evening.

faqs.q: Can we visit Manakamana temple on the way to Pokhara?
faqs.a: Yes. The cable car station at Kurintar is right on the Prithvi Highway, about 3.5–4 hours from Kathmandu. Allow 2–3 hours for the 10-minute ride each way and darshan; on Saturdays and festival days the temple queue can take longer. After the visit, Pokhara is a further 3–3.5 hours by road, so leave Kathmandu by 7 am.

faqs.q: Can I fly directly from India to Pokhara?
faqs.a: Usually not. Pokhara International Airport opened in 2023 and is built for international flights, but scheduled services from India have been rare or seasonal. Most travellers fly Delhi or Kolkata to Kathmandu and connect by a 25-minute domestic flight, or enter by road at Sonauli and drive about 7–8 hours. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Pokhara worth visiting in the monsoon?
faqs.a: It can be, with lowered expectations. From mid-June to early September Pokhara is wet, the mountains are rarely visible and paragliding is mostly paused, but the lake, caves, temples and Mountain Museum remain open, hotel rates drop 25–40 percent and the hills are green. Fly rather than drive, because landslides often delay the highway.
